html:
The Karuk are a Native American people of the middle Klamath River in northwestern California. The Karuk Tribe is one of the largest tribes in the state.

Their name means "upriver people". Salmon runs on the Klamath, acorns and deer fed them, and they managed the forest with deliberate fires. Each year they held world renewal ceremonies to keep the earth in balance. Their language is unrelated to those of their neighbours, the Yurok downstream and the Hupa.

The Gold Rush of the 1850s flooded their land with miners, and they lost most of their land. In the 2000s the Karuk joined other tribes in a long campaign to remove four dams on the Klamath, which had blocked salmon for a century; the dams came down in 2023 and 2024. Their neighbours upriver were the Shasta.
sum: The Karuk are a Native American people of the middle Klamath River in northwestern California. The Karuk Tribe is one of the largest tribes in the state.
